crop.notes: The clipping is the whole 'Short Stops' column of city items; only the paragraph beginning 'Tom Allen denies' (crop piece 3) is about Allen.

ocr.notes: The rest of the column is good, but the Allen paragraph is damaged in the transcript and partly smudged in the image too (the low stake figure and a few words are obscured).

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat reported that Tom Allen denied sending a challenge through Bell's Life to fight Jem Mace, Coburn or anyone for the championship of the world, saying he was now a man of peace and the year-old challenge was void.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Tuesday, November 10, 1874'; the item mentions 'the Democrat'. Before the 1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen denied a report under a New York date that he had sent a challenge to Bell's Life offering to fight Jem Mace, Joe Coburn or any other man for up to $5,000 a side and the championship of the world
Allen said he was now a man of peace and that the challenge referred to, issued nearly a year earlier and never accepted, was void

notes: The lower stake figure is smudged (looks like '$1,000' or '$2,000'); the current summary's '$2,500' is not supported. Only 'Coburn' is printed; Joe Coburn is the likely boxer. Allen's words are reported speech, not a quote.
